components.css: :host{--ink:#14172B;--light:#F4F5F7;--coral:#F0553A;--white:#FFFFFF;--ink-soft:#3A3F5C;--light-soft:#C4C8D8;--rule-light:#D9DCE5;--ease:cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1);} .ds-route{--stem:32px;--r:48px;--left:80px;} .ds-g{position:relative;height:140px;} .ds-gl{background:var(--light);--route:var(--ink);} .ds-gi{background:var(--ink);--route:var(--light);} .ds-stem{position:absolute;top:0;bottom:0;left:var(--left);width:var(--stem);background:var(--route);} .ds-seam{position:absolute;left:calc(var(--left) - var(--r));width:calc(var(--stem) + var(--r) * 2);height:var(--r);} .ds-bottom{bottom:0;} .ds-topf{top:0;} .ds-seam::before,.ds-seam::after{content:'';position:absolute;top:0;width:var(--r);height:var(--r);} .ds-seam::before{left:0;} .ds-seam::after{right:0;} .ds-bottom::before{background:radial-gradient(circle var(--r) at 0 0,transparent calc(100% - .5px),var(--route) 100%);} .ds-bottom::after{background:radial-gradient(circle var(--r) at 100% 0,transparent calc(100% - .5px),var(--route) 100%);} .ds-topf::before{background:radial-gradient(circle var(--r) at 0 100%,transparent calc(100% - .5px),var(--route) 100%);} .ds-topf::after{background:radial-gradient(circle var(--r) at 100% 100%,transparent calc(100% - .5px),var(--route) 100%);}

narrative.overview:
The TutorWays mark is a T whose stem drops and bends into a W. The system treats that stem as a route: one thick stroke, square at its ends, runs down the left of the page from the header to the footer, and every section hangs off it. The header's ink bar is the T's crossbar, centred on the stroke. Each surface the tutor reaches is a stop on the line. Where the page changes ground, the stroke widens into the next ground through quarter-circle fillets, and at the foot of the page the route closes as the TW mark itself.

The world is built from the brand's three avatar grounds (Light, Ink, Coral) used as full-bleed bands in sequence, Outfit ExtraBold display (the wordmark's own face) over Atkinson Hyperlegible text, and hard rectangular geometry everywhere except the curves that belong to the mark. It is plain and confident: big tight headlines, generous vertical rhythm, thin rules between list rows, no ornament that is not the route. Density is low in the narrative and moderate inside the mock product panels, which carry real tutor replies.

Motion follows the stroke. The route draws on with scroll where the browser supports scroll-driven animation, steps activate one at a time as they cross a line near mid-viewport, and every effect has a static, fully drawn fallback.
keyCharacteristics: One stroke, square terminals, weight one sixth of the mark's width, always in the colour that contrasts with its ground.
Three grounds in sequence: Light, Ink, Coral; never a gradient between them.
Every content column aligns to a single left edge set by the stroke.
No rounded corners on any box; the only curves are the mark's semicircles and the fillets.
Coral is scarce: the Ferret ground, the one final primary action, the active stop, the focus ring.

rules.name: The Contrast Stroke Rule
rules.body: The stroke always takes the colour that contrasts with its ground: Ink on Light and Coral, Light on Ink. Each ground sets `--route`, `--soft` and `--rule` together; components read those, never a fixed colour.

rules.name: The Scarce Coral Rule
rules.body: Inside Light and Ink sections Coral marks only the active stop and focus. It becomes a ground once (Ferret) and a button once (the closing primary action). Coral is never used for text on Light or Ink.

rules.name: The Wordmark Voice Rule
rules.body: Every heading is Outfit 800 with negative tracking (about -0.02em) and balanced wrapping. Outfit at 500 and 700 is reserved for navigation and actions; it never sets paragraphs.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Labels are short, bold, sentence case and sit inside the content they describe. No uppercase tracking, no labels floating above headlines.

rules.name: The One Edge Rule
rules.body: All section content aligns to the column set by the stroke. Nothing starts at the gutter except the header's nav and the footer's right-hand links.

rules.name: The Flat Route Rule
rules.body: The stroke, the grounds, the header bar, buttons and stops are never shadowed. Lift is for the mock product panels and tour cards only.

rules.name: The Mark's Curves Rule
rules.body: A curve is allowed only if it is one of the mark's own: its semicircles, or the quarter-circle fillet where the stroke meets a ground (pending confirmation). No border-radius on boxes, no pill buttons, no rounded cards.

rules.name: The Square Terminal Rule
rules.body: The stroke ends square, as the mark's strokes do. It is never capped round.

dos: Do run one square-ended stroke (stem, clamp 14 to 56px) down the page at the same left offset in every section, coloured by the ground (Ink on Light and Coral, Light on Ink).
Do align every section's content to the column set by the stroke.
Do set grounds as full-bleed bands of Light, Ink or Coral, each setting its own route, soft and rule colours.
Do set every heading in Outfit 800 with about -0.02em tracking; set running text in Atkinson Hyperlegible at 1.125rem / 1.55.
Do keep every box square (0px) and use heavy structural borders (2px frames, 3px action underlines, 4px stops).
Do use Coral for the active stop, the focus ring, the Ferret ground and the single closing primary action.
Do ship a static, fully drawn fallback for every scroll effect, and honour reduced motion.
Do use the route ease (`cubic-bezier(.16, 1, .3, 1)`) for state movement.
donts: Don't round any box corner or use pill shapes; curves come only from the mark (its semicircles and the stroke's fillets).
Don't cap the stroke round or draw it thin; it carries the mark's weight.
Don't set Coral text on Light or Ink, or use Coral as decoration inside Light and Ink sections.
Don't shadow the stroke, grounds, header bar, buttons or stops; drop shadows belong to mock product panels and tour cards.
Don't blend grounds with gradients; ground changes are hard edges met by the stroke's fillets.
Don't add uppercase tracked labels above headlines.
narrative.pending: Fillet rule awaits user confirmation: the direction contract originally specified U-bends; the build ships quarter-circle fillets.
